subject: Copywriting
title: Heritage as Copy
description: A quick win: understand Heritage as Copy.

hook.text: 'Founded in 1837.' Hermès doesn't need to explain quality—187 years of history speaks for itself. Heritage sells.

buildup.text: Luxury brands reference founding dates, original craftsmen, and ancestral techniques.

discovery.text: Louis Vuitton's copy mentions its trunk-making origins in every campaign. The story of 1854 Paris is retold endlessly.

climax.text: Real or curated, heritage copy works because humans trust old things.

punchline.text: Founded in 1837. Five digits that justify thousands in price.

quiz.question: Why does heritage work as luxury copy?
options: Longevity implies quality that survived competition

details.summary: Luxury brands weaponize their history. 'Since 1837' isn't just a date — it's a trust signal that implies generations of expertise, consistency, and enduring taste. Heritage copy weaves founding stories, artisan traditions, and historical milestones into narrative proof that the brand has earned...
details.whyItMatters: Heritage solves luxury's credibility problem. Anyone can claim quality; few can back it with 200 years of proof. Understanding heritage storytelling teaches writers to use history as a persuasive tool.
takeaways: Founding dates and origin stories serve as trust and quality signals
Heritage narratives justify premium pricing through implied expertise
Even young brands create heritage through founder stories and craftsmanship

faq.question: How do luxury brands use heritage in copy?
faq.answer: They reference founding dates, artisan lineages, historical patrons (royalty, celebrities), and specific milestones. Patek Philippe's 'You never actually own a Patek Philippe. You merely look after it for the next generation' turns heritage into philosophy — the watch transcends the individual...

faq.question: Can new brands create a sense of heritage?
faq.answer: Yes — through founder stories, sourcing provenance, and craftsmanship narratives. Tesla has no heritage in years, but Elon Musk's founder story and the brand's innovation narrative create a different kind of legacy. Heritage is about credible backstory, not just age.
